title: When the Trail Wakes
premise: Ansel Yarrow, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate, salvages a river-borne chest bearing the seal of Kestria, a nation erased from maps forty years ago. Inside are documents proving a hidden treasury — and a compass that points not north but toward memory. Hunted by the Syndicate's collectors and a Kestrian exile who claims the chest as her birthright, Ansel and his ragtag chase crew must cross the Serrano Range ahead of the snows, racing a monsoon that will close every pass. Betrayal fractures the crew at the high col, where Ansel learns the compass responds to what he's spent five years outrunning: the family he lost in the flood that made him a drifter. In the end he surrenders the treasury to the exiles rather than the Syndicate, pays his debt with the only currency left — testimony — and discovers that found family was never something he had to chase.
about_author: Quentin Blackwood is the pen name of a former field meteorologist who traded radar screens for road atlases and never quite stopped chasing weather on foot. They write adventure novels from a converted storm-spotting van parked somewhere new each season.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Ansel Yarrow chases a supercell across the flats to earn footage money for the Vane Syndicate, narrating his five years of measuring life in miles. His crew — mechanic Odile, navigator Pemba, and rookie Teo — patch the truck as creditors circle. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: restless competence masking dread.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: After flash flooding, Ansel wades the swollen Alder River to recover his drowned instruments and instead hooks a bronze-stamped chest from a snag. The seal belongs to Kestria, a nation wiped from every atlas. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: wonder breaking through cynicism.

chapters.title: A Dead Nation's Signature
chapters.summary: Odile picks the chest's lock; inside are ledgers, a sealed letter, and a brass compass whose needle ignores north. Pemba recognizes Kestrian script from his grandmother's stories. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: giddy discovery curdling into fear of what it will cost them.

chapters.title: Collectors
chapters.summary: Syndicate enforcer Maro Vance arrives early on their debt, sniffing rumors of salvage rights. He offers to forgive everything for the chest. Ansel lies badly. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the trap closing, old debts suddenly lethal.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Refused to Be Erased
chapters.summary: Ilse Marchetti, a Kestrian exile historian, tracks them down and claims the chest by bloodright, showing papers that match its ledgers. She warns that others hunt it too. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: fierce, wounded pride meeting strangers' suspicion.

chapters.title: Compass of Small Truths
chapters.summary: Testing the compass, they realize its needle swings toward places tied to each holder's memories. For Ansel it drags toward the valley where his family drowned. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: eerie intimacy; the object knows them.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Cornered between Vance and a rival salvage ring, the crew votes to run for the Kestrian archive rumored beyond the Serrano Range, ahead of the snows and the coming monsoon. POV: Pemba. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment; a crew becomes an expedition.

chapters.title: Miles Instead of Years
chapters.summary: On the road, Ansel teaches Teo storm-reading while dodging Syndicate spotter planes. Flashbacks reveal the flood that killed his family and the debt he took to bury it. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: grief surfacing in the rearview mirror.

chapters.title: The Last Honest Town
chapters.summary: Resupply in Corvane turns into a standoff when Vance posts their descriptions. A retired ferrywoman shelters them, having once smuggled Kestrian refugees. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: unexpected kindness in hostile territory.

chapters.title: Foothills, First Snow Smell
chapters.summary: They enter the range as the monsoon's outer bands arrive early. Ilse deciphers the letter: the treasury is real, and her grandfather hid it to rebuild Kestria someday. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: hope as a heavy inheritance.

chapters.title: The Rival Ring
chapters.summary: The Calloway salvage team ambushes them at a river ford; Teo is nearly lost crossing. They escape but lose half their supplies. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: terror, then the first taste of belonging when the crew refuses to leave him.

chapters.title: Needle Toward Home
chapters.summary: Stormbound in a cave, the compass pulls Ansel toward a ridge above his drowned hometown. He confesses the truth: the flood that orphaned him was caused by a Syndicate dam failure he helped survey. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Vance at the Treeline
chapters.summary: Maro Vance catches them with hired mountain men. Odile sabotages his snowcat; the fight scatters the group across the treeline. Pemba is taken. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: fury and guilt; the cost of running made flesh.

chapters.title: Split Trail
chapters.summary: With the pass closing, they split: Ilse and Teo push for the col while Ansel and Odile track Vance's camp to free Pemba. POV: alternating via letters left at a cairn. Emotional beat: trust tested by distance.

chapters.title: Camp of Borrowed Fires
chapters.summary: Infiltrating Vance's camp, Ansel finds Pemba unbroken and learns Vance's own secret: he's a Kestrian descendant selling the treasury back to the Syndicate to buy his family out of servitude. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: hatred complicated by recognition.

chapters.title: The Col Before the Snows
chapters.summary: Reunited, they race the final ascent as the monsoon makes landfall below. Avalanche danger forces them onto the exposed knife ridge. POV: Pemba. Emotional beat: exhausted solidarity against indifferent weather.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the High Col
chapters.summary: Calloway's surviving scout, embedded since the ford, steals the chest and cuts the rope line. Teo falls; Ansel goes down after him against all sense. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the vertigo of being chosen over treasure.

chapters.title: What the Compass Wanted
chapters.summary: Stranded on a glacier shelf, Ansel follows the needle to a crevasse cache — his father's old survey kit, hidden before the flood. The compass has been leading him home all along. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: devastating clarity; memory as terrain.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Archive
chapters.summary: They reach the Kestrian archive vault as the full monsoon hits. Vance arrives not to fight but to surrender his claim, asking only that his name be struck from the Syndicate's ledger. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: enemies laid bare by shared exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Treasury
chapters.summary: Inside the vault: gold, records, and the names of the erased. Ansel refuses to sell; the treasury goes to the exile community, with evidence of the dam failure aimed at the Syndicate. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: power declined is power redeemed.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Descending through the storm, Ansel gives sworn testimony about the dam, trading his silence for the erasure of his debts. Vance corroborates. The Syndicate's optimists begin to fold. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the terrible relief of telling the truth.

chapters.title: When the Trail Wakes
chapters.summary: Spring: the crew repairs the truck, Ilse sends word that Kestrians are rebuilding, and the compass now points nowhere at all — its work done. Ansel stops measuring life in miles. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; found family, finally home.
